annotation.title_clean: Designing a Novel Robot Activist Model for Interactive Child Rights Education
annotation.title_en: Designing a Novel Robot Activist Model for Interactive Child Rights Education
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Chew, E.; Khan, U.S.; Lee, P.H.
named_instruments_referenced: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
annotation.summary_en: Journal article describing the design and deployment of a NAO-based 'Robot Activist' for child rights education in Malaysian schools, in partnership between SUHAKAM (the national human rights institution) and Monash University Malaysia. It reports phased pilot interactions, constraints and recommendations; it is not a governance document.
key_provisions_or_claims: NAO humanoid robot used to teach the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child via Q&A and Simon Says game
Robot is intended to extend, not replace, human educators
Phased pilots led to fewer questions and a performance-tracking feature to sustain children's attention
Cost-effectiveness of educational robots is a key constraint
Recommendations proposed for the next phase of model design
